title: Cheese, Genever and the North Holland Table
subRegion: North Holland and the Schiedam distilleries

bestPeriod.note: The Alkmaar and Edam demonstration markets run April to September, and Hollandse Nieuwe herring reaches the stalls from late May or early June.

summary: A week from Amsterdam's brown cafés to Alkmaar's cheese-carrier guild and Schiedam's tall malt-mill distilleries, timed to the new herring season.
hook: This week runs on three engines: cheese, grain spirit and the North Sea. Alkmaar's cheese carriers still work the Waagplein in white uniforms and coloured guild hats; Schiedam's windmills were built absurdly tall for one reason, to catch wind over the malt-house roofs for jenever distilling; and Amsterdam ties it together with a herring cart on every other corner once the new season starts.

snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 120 km of train travel across the week; flat city and polder walking throughout
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Amsterdam Schiphol (AMS), direct train to Amsterdam Centraal, approx. 20 minutes
snapshot.Who It Suits: Cheese and spirits obsessives, herring-season completists, anyone happy eating standing up

itinerary.title: Amsterdam, brown cafés and herring
itinerary.morning: Land at Schiphol and train to Amsterdam Centraal, about 20 minutes. Drop bags near the Jordaan.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Jordaan's canals and find a bruine kroeg, a "brown café" named for decades of tobacco-stained walls, for an orientation Genever borrel, poured to the brim in a tulip glass, traditionally sipped without lifting it first.
itinerary.evening: Broodje haring at a herring cart if the new season (Hollandse Nieuwe) has started; if not, order the cured, onion-topped version instead, and bitterballen with mustard as a bar snack.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 0. Km travelled: 4 km on foot. Approx. tasting spend: €0.

itinerary.title: Albert Cuypmarkt and craft jenever
itinerary.morning: The Albert Cuypmarkt in De Pijp runs Monday to Saturday, roughly 09:00-17:00, the country's largest daily street market, cheese stalls, stroopwafel griddles, and produce from the polders sit side by side.
itinerary.afternoon: A. van Wees "De Ooievaar," a small working jenever distillery in the Jordaan, still distils on-site and runs walk-in tastings through its tiny proeflokaal (tasting room), though a guided tour is best booked a day ahead by email.
itinerary.evening: Kaassoufflé, a deep-fried cheese-filled pastry, and a jenever tasting flight comparing jonge (young, neutral) against oude (old, malty) styles.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 1. Km travelled: 6 km. Approx. tasting spend: €20-30.

itinerary.title: North to Alkmaar
itinerary.morning: Train from Amsterdam Centraal to Alkmaar, about 35 minutes. Check into Alkmaar and walk the Waagplein.
itinerary.afternoon: If it is a Friday between April and early September, the Alkmaar cheese market runs 10:00-13:00, worth stressing plainly: this is a seasonal demonstration for visitors, staged by the historic cheese-carriers' guild on the Waagplein, not a working wholesale trade (that moved to closed auction decades ago). The ceremony is still genuine: guild members in white with coloured straw hats carry wheels on wooden barrows, weigh them at the 14th-century Waaggebouw, and settle the price with a ritual hand-clap.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Alkmaar; smoked eel if a stall or restaurant has it, with a young Dutch Gouda to compare against the market wheels.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 0. Km travelled: 4 km. Approx. tasting spend: €15-20.

itinerary.title: Edam and the smaller market
itinerary.morning: Train and bus (or a direct regional bus) to Edam, about 45 minutes from Alkmaar. Edam runs its own, smaller cheese demonstration market on Wednesdays in July and August, roughly 10:30-12:30, on Jan van Nieuwenhuizenplein, again a folkloric event rather than a trading market, on a shorter season than Alkmaar's.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk Edam's canals and the Grote Kerk; a working cheese farm near Volendam, such as the well-known Catharina Hoeve, gives a hands-on demonstration of traditional Edam-making outside market hours.
itinerary.evening: Back to Alkmaar. A plate of Dutch cheeses by age, jong, belegen, oud, tasted side by side.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 1. Km travelled: 8 km plus transfers. Approx. tasting spend: €15-20.

itinerary.title: Volendam, Marken and North Sea fish
itinerary.morning: A short bus or boat hop from Edam to Volendam, the old fishing harbour on the IJsselmeer, still selling smoked eel (paling) straight off the boats.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to Marken, a former island village of green-black wooden houses, on foot along the causeway or by the seasonal ferry from Volendam. The contrast between the two, Volendam loud and commercial, Marken quiet, is the point.
itinerary.evening: Return to Amsterdam by train via Amsterdam Centraal. Settle into the second Amsterdam base with a North Sea seafood dinner, mussels or plaice, depending on the season.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 0. Km travelled: 12 km plus transfers. Approx. tasting spend: €20-25.

itinerary.title: Schiedam, city of tall mills
itinerary.morning: Train from Amsterdam to Schiedam Centrum, about an hour. Schiedam's skyline is genuinely unusual: its windmills, including De Noord and De Vrijheid, are among the tallest traditional mills in the world, built that height specifically to catch clean wind over the malt-house roofs that once ringed the town.
itinerary.afternoon: The Nationaal Jenevermuseum, housed in a former distillery on the Lange Haven, covers the malt-wine spirit's full history. Nolet's Distillery, family-run since 1691 and still producing genever alongside its better-known vodka, offers the House of Nolet visitor experience by advance booking only, reserve online at least a week ahead, more in summer.
itinerary.evening: Dinner back in Amsterdam; a last jenever, this time an oude style, with Kachkéis-style farm cheese and rye bread.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 1-2 (Nolet reservation-dependent). Km travelled: 6 km plus transfers. Approx. tasting spend: €20-30.

itinerary.title: Amsterdam market close and departure
itinerary.morning: A last pass through the Albert Cuypmarkt or the Noordermarkt farmers' market (Saturdays, roughly 09:00-16:00) for cheese and preserves to take home.
itinerary.afternoon: A canal walk through the Nine Streets, then the train to Schiphol.
itinerary.dayStats: Cellars visited: 0. Km travelled: 5 km plus airport transfer. Approx. tasting spend: €10-15.

accommodationStrategy.name: The Hoxton, Amsterdam
accommodationStrategy.description: A well-known, centrally placed hotel in a row of converted canal houses, close to the Nine Streets, De Pijp trams and the train to both Alkmaar and Schiedam, a practical hub for a week built on day trips.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 8 weeks ahead for May and September.

accommodationStrategy.name: NH Alkmaar
accommodationStrategy.description: A short walk from the Waagplein and the station, useful for being inside the old town before the market crowds arrive on a Friday morning and for the short hop to Edam and Volendam.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6 weeks ahead, earlier for a market Friday.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; the Netherlands uses 112 for all services.
logistics.bookingWindows: The House of Nolet tour in Schiedam is by advance reservation only, made online; walk-ins are not accommodated.
logistics.money: Cards, including contactless, are near-universal in the Netherlands; some very small stalls are card-only, the reverse of much of Europe.

other.label: The Alkmaar and Edam markets are demonstrations, not trade
other.text: Alkmaar's runs Fridays only, April to early September, 10:00-13:00; Edam's runs Wednesdays only, July and August, 10:30-12:30. Both are seasonal and weather can shorten a session; check the tourist board's calendar before travelling for one specifically.

other.label: Trains
other.text: NS regional trains connect Amsterdam, Alkmaar and Schiedam directly and frequently; buy an OV-chipkaart or use contactless bank card tap-in/tap-out on all trains, trams and buses.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Many Amsterdam shops open late on Sunday and Monday mornings; cheese farms outside the main towns often close for a midday break.

other.label: Drink-drive alternatives
other.text: This trip runs entirely on foot, tram and train; there is no driving leg, so the only rule is timing trains around tastings rather than rushing between them.

proTips: Arrive in Alkmaar the night before a Friday market and walk the empty Waagplein at 08:00, the guild sets up in the hour before the ceremony starts.

Ask a herring cart to serve it "Hollandse Nieuwe" only once the season is confirmed open, usually late May or early June; earlier in the year it is last year's catch, still good but a different thing.
Book A. van Wees's guided distillery tour a day ahead by email; the walk-in proeflokaal is available without booking but the tour explains the copper stills.
Reserve Nolet's House of Nolet the moment dates are fixed, slots in June and September fill weeks out.

Compare Edam and Alkmaar cheese: Edam is traditionally the smaller, ball-shaped export cheese with a red wax coat; Alkmaar's market historically traded the flatter, larger Gouda-style wheels, which is why Alkmaar's ceremony is the bigger of the two.
Catch the Noordermarkt farmers' market on Saturday morning for organic and small-producer cheese away from the tourist stalls.

packingNotes: Comfortable, flat shoes; Amsterdam and market-town cobbles punish anything else.
A rain shell that packs small, North Sea weather turns quickly even in June.
A small cooler bag or vacuum-seal option for cheese or smoked eel to take home.
Cash in small notes for herring carts and market stalls, even though cards work almost everywhere else.
A tote or basket bag; Dutch markets expect you to bring your own.
Sunglasses; the flat polder light off the IJsselmeer is sharper than it looks on a grey forecast.
whatCouldGoWrong: **You arrive expecting Alkmaar's market to be a real trading floor.** It closed as a wholesale market long ago; go for the guild ceremony and the atmosphere, not for wholesale prices.
**Nolet's Distillery is fully booked.** The Nationaal Jenevermuseum in the same town gives comparable historical depth without a reservation.
**The herring season hasn't started yet.** Cured herring and smoked eel are available year-round at the same stalls.
**Rain washes out Marken or Volendam.** Both have enough covered cafés and the Marken church and Volendam's fishing museum to fill an hour.

**A market Friday or Wednesday falls outside the April-September window.** Alkmaar and Edam's cheese farms, including Catharina Hoeve near Volendam, run demonstrations independent of the town market calendar.
